q: How do I measure the energy saved by changing a cold store's temperature set point?
title: Cold store set point energy saving
short: Change the set point only within the product's quality limit, then compare the sub-metered kWh with a period of similar load and weather, and convert the difference at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh. Report the measured figure with dates, not a rule-of-thumb percentage.
audience: Cold storage and frozen food warehouse operators

p: Frozen and chilled products have temperature limits set by food safety and buyer specifications. Any change must stay within them, with records.
Defrost frequency, condenser cleaning and door seals also affect use. Measure each change separately where you can.

example.title: Worked example: two comparable months (illustrative inputs)
lines: At -18 C (June, similar load): 39,500 kWh x 0.710 = 28,045 kg CO2
Measured difference: 1,775 kg CO2 a month
Check product quality limits before any change
example.note: Readings are illustrative; use your sub-meter and temperature logs.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
